# local 0008: Arithmetic on the address of an element of a nested array of function pointers steps by a row

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: In geniCodeArray and geniCodeAddressOf, give &fp[i][j] the type pointer to element when the elements are function pointers.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

When an array of function pointers is an array element or a struct member, the address of one of
its elements has the type pointer to that array. Arithmetic on the address and indexing through
it step by a row. The file below was compiled on r17176 with `sdcc -mmcs51 p2.c` and run
in ucsim.

```c
void (*fp[2][2]) (void);
unsigned char guard[2];

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[5];

void h (void) { }
void set (void) { (&fp[1][0])[1] = h; }
int diff (void) { return &fp[1][1] - &fp[0][1]; }

void main (void)
{
  set ();
  res[0] = (fp[1][1] == h);
  res[1] = (&fp[1][0] + 1 == &fp[1][1]);
  res[2] = diff ();
  res[3] = guard[0];
  res[4] = guard[1];
  for (;;);
}
```

After the run `res` holds `00 00 01 a9 00`, and `01 01 02 00 00` is expected. `set` is compiled to
`mov ((_fp + 0x0008) + 0),#_h` and `mov ((_fp + 0x0008) + 1),#(_h >> 8)`. The element `fp[1][1]`
is at `_fp + 6`. `_fp + 8` is the first byte after the array, where the linker placed `guard`, and
`a9 00` is the address of `h`. `diff` returns 1.

The result is `00 00 01 a9 00` with `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, `--stack-auto`, and
`--model-large --stack-auto` too. Compiled with `-mstm8 -c` and with `-mz80 -c`, the statement in
`set` also writes to `_fp + 8`. With `--model-huge`, where a function pointer has 3 bytes,
`&fp[1][0] + 1` is compiled to `_fp + 12`, and `_fp + 9` is expected.

Other expressions were compiled for mcs51 with the small model and read in the assembly. For
`struct s { char c; void (*m[2]) (void); } st;`, `(&st.m[0])[1] = h` writes to `_st + 5`, where
`_st + 3` is expected, and `&st.m[1] - &st.m[0]` is computed as 0. `&fp[i][0] + j` scales `j` by
4, and an element has 2 bytes. A one-dimensional array that is a variable,
`void (*fp1[4]) (void);`, is correct for `(&fp1[1])[1]`, `&fp1[i] + j`, and `&fp1[3] - &fp1[1]`.

## Cause

The cause was read from the source and from the iCode that `--dump-i-code` writes. No patch was
tried.

`geniCodeArray` in `src/SDCCicode.c` gives the operand for an array element the type of the
array when the elements are function pointers. The condition is
`IS_ARRAY (ltype) && IS_FUNCPTR (ltype->next)`, which r9456 added with the fix for bug #2455.
`geniCodeAddressOf` then makes a pointer to the type of the operand. In the iCode for
`&fp[i][0] + j`, the address has the type pointer to `void (*[2]) (void)`, and `j` is shifted
left by 2. For `&fp1[i] + j` the type is pointer to `void (*) (void)`, and `j` is shifted by 1.

## Related

Bug #2691 concerns `&a[i][j]` for nested arrays of object pointers. Its patch adds a condition to
the branch of `geniCodeAddressOf` for operands of pointer type. The operands here have an array
type, so the patch does not change this defect, which was found with the test cases of that bug.
